title: STEP and IGES
cards/0/title: STEP: the common language of engineering
cards/0/body:
STEP is the international standard ISO 10303. Every serious CAD system understands it: SolidWorks, CATIA, NX, Creo, Inventor, Fusion, FreeCAD.

It holds exact surfaces (B-rep, NURBS) and assemblies, and the AP242 protocol adds dimensions and tolerances right on the model (PMI).
cards/0/deep: Application protocols (APs) are different “dialects” of STEP. AP203 is the design 3D model, AP214 is automotive (added colors and layers), and AP242 merged them and added PMI and data for drawing-free manufacturing (MBD).
cards/1/body: It is text. Each line is an entity with its own number, and it refers to other numbers.
cards/2/q: Which line sets the 50 mm radius?
cards/2/explain: CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE(name, placement, radius) is our “cylinder with a 50 radius”.
cards/3/options/0: #12, the cylinder’s coordinate system: a point and an axis direction
cards/3/explain: #12 in turn refers to point #10 and direction #11. That is how STEP builds a model from small linked pieces.
cards/4/body:
IGES appeared in the US in 1980 and was the main exchange format for a long time. The last version is 5.3 (1996).

It carries surfaces, but often handles solids and assemblies badly: after import you get “surfaces without a solid” that have to be stitched together. Today people use STEP instead.
cards/5/q: You imported an IGES and got a pile of separate surfaces with no volume. Why?
cards/5/options/0: IGES often carries only surfaces without solid topology; you have to stitch them or use STEP
cards/5/explain: Without topology the program does not know the surfaces form a closed solid.
cards/6/q: What can STEP AP242 carry? Select all.
cards/6/options/2: Dimensions and tolerances on the model (PMI)
cards/6/explain: STEP is about engineering, not games.
cards/7/q: A contractor asks for a part model “in a neutral format”. What do you send?
cards/7/explain: STEP keeps the exact geometry, and it can be edited further in any CAD system. STL is just triangles.
cards/8/pairs/3/1: Dimensions and tolerances on the model
